key_insight: Scaling test-time compute in embodied planners is not always better: it raises latency, token use, and FLOPs, but the gains in task success are uneven and often diminish. The paper argues that the real challenge is deciding when and where extra compute is worth spending.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the inefficiency of blindly increasing test-time compute for Vision-Language Models used as high-level planners in embodied agents, where higher compute can reduce deployability without reliably improving performance.
method: Analyzes how allocating more test-time compute affects embodied planning performance, latency, token usage, and FLOPs.
Focuses on identifying the conditions under which compute spending improves downstream success versus when it produces diminishing returns.
Frames test-time compute as a resource-allocation problem: deciding when and where to spend compute for frontier performance in real-world deployment.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work highlights that better planning performance may come from smarter compute allocation rather than more compute overall. It provides a practical lens for building embodied systems that are faster, cheaper, and more deployable.
visual_elements: A trade-off chart showing test-time compute vs. success rate, latency, and FLOPs

paper_title: DIRECT: When and Where Should You Allocate Test-Time Compute in Embodied Planners?
paper_authors: Jadelynn Dao, Milan Ganai, Yasmina Abukhadra, Ajay Sridhar, Mozhgan Nasr Azadani
